newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say refugee outpost is not a target.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say refugee outpost is not a target.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Tuesday an eastern town where tens of thousands of Hutu refugees have fled is not a target for their military advance.
Since the weekend Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees have been flooding into Ubundu, 100 km (60 miles) southeast of Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city and the main rebel objective.

"Ubundu is not a target, we have no intention of attacking refugees and have given the international community every facility to set up a humanitarian corridor that will allow the refugees to go home," said Bizima Karaha, foreign affairs commissar of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire.

United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees spokesman Paul Stromberg said that local staff who visited Ubundu late on Monday estimated that at least 40,000 refugees had gathered there on the banks of the Zaire river.
"Most of them are men, which is likely to be because they were stronger than women and children and we believe thousands more are likely to emerge from the forest," Stromberg said.
He added that the UNHCR planned to deliver 12 tonnes of supplies on Wednesday from Kisangani if the security situation allowed it.
Rebel Voice of the People radio said Kisangani was surrounded and AFDL fighters had advanced to within 10 km (six miles) of the town.
A spokeswoman for the World Food Programme on Monday said the refugees at Ubundu were afraid of further rebel advances and wanted to move on.

The Hutu refugees have fled ever further westwards into Zaire since the AFDL launched its rebellion in October with a force spearheaded by ethnic Tutsis. They live in fear of reprisals for Rwanda's 1994 genocide of at least 800,000 minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
U.N. agencies this week plan to set up a base at Tingi Tingi, a camp deserted last month by 170,000 people, to encourage refugees to come out of the forest for eventual repatriation.
